t: A kingdom of western Mexico centred on Lake Pátzcuaro, ruled from Tzintzuntzan by a king the Spaniards called the cazonci.
In the late 1470s it routed an Aztec army led by Axayacatl, and the Aztecs never conquered it.
Its smiths led Mesoamerica in copper and bronze; it submitted to Spain in 1522, and its last king was executed in 1530.
dyk: The Relación de Michoacán, the main source for the kingdom’s history, was illustrated with 44 paintings by Purépecha artists and is kept today in the royal library of El Escorial in Spain.
ev: Tariácuri unites the communities of the Lake Pátzcuaro basin
Power is concentrated at Tzintzuntzan, the kingdom’s only true city
Purépecha forces rout the Aztec army of Axayacatl near Taximaroa
King Zuangua dies, probably of smallpox, and Tangaxuan II succeeds him
Cristóbal de Olid enters Tzintzuntzan and Tangaxuan II submits to Spain
Nuño de Guzmán has Tangaxuan II executed on 14 February
Vasco de Quiroga is appointed the first bishop of Michoacán

f.capital: Pátzcuaro; later also Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan; Tzintzuntzan alone from the mid-15th century
